Testi kebab (pottery kebab): Salt, black pepper, thyme (1 dessert spoon salt)
1 clay jug; a handful of dough or foil to seal the top
Soak the jug in water for at least 1 hour.
Mix the meat, onions, garlic, chopped tomato and pepper, tomato paste, butter and spices.
Fill the jug with the mixture; seal the top tightly with dough or foil.
Put the jug in a cold oven, set to 220 °C and cook for 2.5 hours.
Take out of the oven, carefully break the jug near the neck and serve with rice.
Don’t put the jug into a hot oven; the sudden change in temperature cracks it.
Water pudding (with rose water)
1 tablespoon icing sugar for the top
Dissolve the cornflour in some of the cold water without lumps.
Put the remaining water and sugar in a pan and add the cornflour.
Cook over a medium heat, stirring constantly, for 10–12 minutes until thick and translucent.
Add the rose water and divide among wet bowls.
Once cool, sprinkle with icing sugar and serve.
Şalgam (fermented purple carrot drink, homemade)
2 purple carrots
1 turnip
3 litres water
2 tablespoons rock salt
1 dessert spoon chilli flakes (optional)
Put the bulgur in a cloth bag and leave in 1 litre lukewarm water for 1 day to sour.
Wash the purple carrots and turnip, chop roughly and put in a glass jar.
Add the soured bulgur water, the remaining water and the salt to the jar.
Cover the top with muslin and ferment in a cool place for 5–7 days until it tastes sour.
Strain and keep in the fridge; serve cold.
Check the jar every day; if you see mould, throw it away.
1 week in a sealed bottle in the fridge.
Homemade boza (fermented grain drink)
4 litres water
1 dessert spoon dried yeast
For the top: 1 dessert spoon cinnamon and 3 tablespoons roasted chickpeas
Wash the bulgur and rice and cook in 2 litres water for 1 hour until completely broken down.
Blend and pass through a fine sieve; add the remaining water to reach a pourable consistency.
When lukewarm, stir in the yeast; cover and leave at room temperature for 2 days.
Stir in the sugar and rest in the fridge for 1 more day.
Serve with cinnamon and roasted chickpeas.
It is a fermented drink; give it only in moderation to young children and pregnant women, and don’t drink boza that has gone sour.
Mücendere (lentil rice with caramelised onions)
Salt, cumin (1 dessert spoon salt)
Boil the lentils in 3 cups water for 15 minutes until half-tender.
Add the washed rice, salt and 1 cup hot water and cook over a low heat until the liquid is absorbed.
Slice the onions thinly and fry in olive oil for 15 minutes until dark brown.
Mix half the onions into the rice and put the rest on top.
Serve warm or at room temperature with yogurt.
Yuvalama soup (tiny meatball yogurt soup)
500 g lamb (on the bone)
For the yuvalama: 200 g lean mince
1 cup rice flour
1 kg strained yogurt
1 tablespoon dried mint
Boil and shred the meat; strain the stock.
Make chickpea-sized balls from a mixture of mince, rice flour, salt and water added little by little.
Cook the yuvalama in the stock for 10 minutes; add the chickpeas and meat.
Whisk the yogurt, egg and flour, temper with a few ladles of hot stock and add to the pot.
Cook, stirring constantly, until it boils; add salt.
Sizzle the mint in butter and drizzle over the top.
It is a festive dish of Gaziantep; the smaller the yuvalama, the better.
Analı kızlı (“mother and daughter” köfte soup)
For the “mother” köfte: 200 g lean mince, 1 cup fine bulgur, 1 dessert spoon tomato paste
For the filling: 150 g mince, 1 onion, 2 tablespoons walnuts
For the “daughters”: about 1 cup of the same dough set aside
1 egg, 1 tablespoon flour
2 tablespoons butter, dried mint, salt
Soak the bulgur and knead with the mince and tomato paste into a dough that doesn’t stick to your hands.
Fry the mince with the onion and add the walnuts to make the filling.
Hollow out walnut-sized pieces of dough and fill them with the filling (mothers); make small balls from the rest of the dough with no filling (daughters).
Cook the mothers and daughters with the chickpeas in salted water for 15 minutes.
Whisk the yogurt, egg and flour, temper and add, stirring until it boils.
Drizzle with mint butter and serve.
Keşkek (pounded wheat and meat)
2 cups whole wheat for aşure (soaked overnight)
1 kg lamb or chicken on the bone
Discard the soaking water and boil the wheat in fresh water for 1 hour.
Boil the meat in a separate pot, skimming off the foam, until it falls off the bone; shred.
Cook the wheat with the meat stock over a low heat for 2 hours until it completely breaks down.
Add the meat and beat constantly with a wooden spoon to get a thick, stretchy consistency; add salt.
Transfer to a plate and drizzle with butter sizzled with chilli flakes.
It is on UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage list; a dish for weddings and festivals.
Hingel (potato dumplings)
For the dough: 2 cups flour
For the filling: 3 boiled potatoes
For the sauce: 1.5 cups garlic yogurt, 2 tablespoons butter, 1 onion, 1 dessert spoon chilli flakes
Knead the dough and rest for 30 minutes.
Mash the potatoes and mix with fried onion, parsley and spices.
Roll out the dough thinly and cut rounds with a glass.
Put filling on each round, fold into a half-moon and press the edges.
Boil in salted water; once they rise to the surface, cook 3 more minutes and drain.
Serve with garlic yogurt and butter with onion and chilli flakes.
The potato mantı of Caucasian and Eastern Anatolian cuisine.
Dry köfte (pan-fried meatballs)
Crumb of 2 slices stale bread
1 cup sunflower oil for frying
3 tablespoons flour for coating
Soak and squeeze the bread; knead all the ingredients well for 5 minutes.
Rest the mixture in the fridge for 30 minutes.
With wet hands, make flat, oval walnut-sized köfte.
Dust lightly with flour and fry in hot oil for 6–8 minutes until browned on both sides.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve with piyaz (bean salad) or potatoes.
Chicken broth soup
2 chicken thighs (on the bone)
Half a cup vermicelli or rice
Boil the chicken in 2 litres water for 45 minutes, skimming the foam; shred and strain the stock.
Toast the flour in butter and add the chicken stock.
Add the grated carrot and vermicelli and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the chicken meat and season with salt and black pepper.
Temper the egg yolk and lemon, add them and remove from the heat without boiling.
A good option to support fluid intake during illness.
Black cabbage soup
1 bunch black cabbage (collard greens)
1 cup boiled borlotti or haricot beans
Half a cup cornmeal
Salt, chilli flakes (1 dessert spoon salt)
Wash the black cabbage, remove the stalks and chop finely.
Add the black cabbage and 6 cups hot water and cook for 25 minutes.
Add the beans; sprinkle in the cornmeal little by little, stirring.
Cook 10 more minutes and season with salt and chilli flakes.
Typical of Black Sea cuisine; served with cornbread.
